newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-CRONJE CARRIES IRELAND TO BRINK OF VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-CRONJE CARRIES IRELAND TO BRINK OF VICTORY.

text.p: South Africa captain Hansie Cronje hit an unbeaten 94 to carry Ireland to the brink of an upset victory over Middlesex in the Benson and Hedges Cup limited overs competition on Monday.
Cronje, signed to lead Ireland at the bequest of South African cricket chief Ali Bacher, batted at number four and steered his side to an imposing total of 281 for four.
Middlesex were in big trouble at 134 for six off 32.2 of their 50 overs when rain ended play early in Dublin.
Ireland have not won a game since they entered the cup in 1994.
Bacher is also chairman of the International Cricket Council (ICC's) development committee and suggested Cronje play in Ireland as part of a campaign to promote the game globally.
Mark Ealham hit a final ball six to carry Kent to a thrilling four-wicket victory over Surrey at The Oval.
Zimbabwe's Paul Strang and Ealham (19 not out) scampered in the winning 12 runs after opener Matthew Walker (56) and Graham Cowdrey (47) had laid the groundwork for Kent's 262 for six.
England batsman Alec Stewart made the top score of 51 in Surrey's total of 257.
World Cup qualifiers Scotland were brought back to earth by English champions Leicestershire who piled up a cup record 371 for six in Leicester.
Darren Maddy (97) and Iain Sutcliffe (59) smashed an opening stand of 159 in just 25 overs to set the tone for what was to come -- an improvement on Warwickshire's 369 for eight made last season.
Leicestershire's innings included 36 fours and eight sixes.
Scotland, missing eight of their squad which finished third at the ICC Trophy in Malaysia this month to qualify for the 2000 World Cup, were never in contention and lost by 178 runs.
Warwickshire's Dougie Brown took five for 31 to carry his side to a six-wicket victory in a low scoring match against Worcestershire at Worcester.
The medium pacer sent the top order crashing as Worcestershire tumbled to 56 for nine before last wicket pair Stuart Lampitt and Phil Newport put on 40.

Worcestershire finished at 96 all out, after 37.1 overs and then turned around to reduce their opponents to 36 for four. Dominic Ostler (37 not out) and Trevor Penney (33 not out) kept their heads to steer Warwickshire to victory.
Australian Shaun Young (52) and Nicky Trainor (62) guided Gloucestershire to 281 for six and a 122-run victory against British Universities at Bristol.
At Chelmsford, all-rounder Ronnie Irani took three wickets and hit an unbeaten 82 to carry Essex to a five-wicket win over Glamorgan.
Veterans Bill Athey (66) and Paul Jarvis (42 not out) guided Sussex to a 49-run victory against Hampshire at Hove.
The three remaining matches involving Yorkshire and Lancashire, Derbyshire and Minor Counties, and Durham and Nottinghamshire will resume on Tuesday after being interrupted by rain.
